meta.title: How the Laju speed test works
meta.description: A full explanation of the measurement order, the parameters in use, and the limits of a browser-based speed test.

hero.title: How Laju measures your connection
hero.lead: Four steps, published parameters, and an honest list of what the result cannot tell you.

latency.title: 1. Latency and jitter
latency.body: The browser sends a series of tiny, uncacheable requests. The fastest round trip becomes the latency figure, while jitter is the mean difference between consecutive probes. This is HTTP rather than ICMP, so the number reads slightly higher than a ping command.

download.title: 2. Download
download.body: Several parallel connections pull random data from our server and bytes are counted as they land. Random data is used because it cannot be compressed in transit, so nothing inflates the figure.

loaded.title: 3. Latency under load
loaded.body: While the download runs, latency is measured again. A large increase points to over-full buffers somewhere along the path — the usual reason for lag on a line that looks fast.

upload.title: 4. Upload
upload.body: Random data is sent back to the server and discarded on arrival. Browsers report upload progress slightly ahead of the wire, which is why the upload warm-up window is the longer of the two.

parameters.title: The numbers the engine runs on
parameters.lead: These values are read straight from the measurement configuration, so this page always matches what actually runs.

limits.title: What this result cannot tell you
limits.lead: We would rather state the limits than let a number claim more than it can support.

items.singleServer: The test runs against a single server, not a global network. The path to other services may look different.
items.browserOverhead: Measurement happens inside a browser over HTTPS, so there is encryption and processing cost a system-level tool would not pay.
items.wifi: Wi-Fi, tired cabling or an ageing router is often the slowest link, rather than the subscription itself.
items.vpn: A VPN, proxy or network-level ad blocker changes the result because traffic takes an extra path.
items.sharedLine: Other devices using the same connection during the run will pull the numbers down.
items.uploadReporting: Upload progress is reported by the browser from its socket buffers, so the first seconds tend to look faster than reality.

whyDifferent.q: Why does this differ from other speed tests?
whyDifferent.a: Every tool uses different servers, durations, connection counts and averaging rules. Differences of tens of percent between tools are normal. A very large gap usually means the path itself is different — the other tool may test against your operator's nearest server while Laju tests against its own. And when Laju is served from a local server, the payload never leaves your machine at all, so the number is not an internet speed. Comparing results from the same tool over time is far more useful.

ipv6Missing.q: Why is my IPv6 address not detected?
ipv6Missing.a: Usually because your network or provider has not enabled IPv6, or a device along the path blocks it. It is not a fault on your machine; it simply means your traffic still travels over IPv4.

whatIsJitter.a: Jitter is how much the round-trip time changes from one probe to the next. Low jitter means a steady stream; high jitter makes voice and video sound choppy even when throughput is large.

whatIsBufferbloat.a: It is the latency measured while the line is saturated by a download. If it rises far above the idle figure, there are probably over-full buffers in your router or in the provider network.

dataUsage.q: How much data does a test use?
dataUsage.a: It depends on your speed, because the test runs for a fixed time rather than a fixed size. A faster connection moves more data in the same window. The exact amount is shown in the details of every result.

isDataStored.q: Are my results stored on your server?
isDataStored.a: No. The test payload is random bytes that are discarded immediately, and results are kept only in your browser's local storage. You can erase them at any time from the History page.

bestPractice.q: How do I get the most representative result?
bestPractice.a: Close active downloads and streams, use a cable if you can, move closer to the router on Wi-Fi, then run the test a few times at different hours and compare the pattern.

meta.title: About Laju
meta.description: Laju is an independent internet speed test built around transparent methodology and user privacy.

hero.title: A small measuring tool that tries to be honest
hero.lead: Laju exists because too many speed tests show a big number without explaining where it came from, or what it cannot prove.

story.p1: Laju started from a simple need: explaining to someone why a connection sold as fast still feels slow. A download figure alone rarely answers that, because latency and jitter are usually what gets in the way.
story.p2: So every result here comes with its context — when it was measured, against which server, for how long, and over how many parallel connections. The engine parameters are rendered straight from configuration rather than retyped by hand.
story.p3: The project is maintained by one person and is still growing. If you spot a number that looks wrong or an explanation that reads badly, hearing about it genuinely helps.

transparency.title: Open about the method
transparency.body: How the measurement works, which parameters it uses and where it falls short are written on a page anyone can read, not buried in jargon.

privacy.title: As little data as possible
privacy.body: No accounts, no advertising trackers, and results that stay in your browser. The test payload is random bytes the server throws away.

accessibility.title: Usable by everyone
accessibility.body: Colour contrast, keyboard navigation, alternative text and reduced-motion preferences were considered from the start rather than patched on later.

notDoing.title: What we deliberately do not do
notDoing.lead: Just as important as a feature list: the things Laju intentionally leaves out.

items.i1: We do not promise results identical to an operator's own official measurement equipment.
items.i2: We do not store your results on a server or build user profiles.
items.i3: We do not publish provider rankings or comparisons, because our data is not sufficient for that.
items.i4: We do not claim any certification, accreditation or award.

hero.title: Privacy policy
hero.lead: The short version: measurements use random bytes, results stay in your browser, and your IP address is used only to show it back to you.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
Laju is a measurement tool without accounts. We do not ask for a name, phone number or payment details in order to run a test.

This page explains what happens to the technical data that is unavoidable whenever a site is loaded, such as the IP address that every server you contact can see.

whatWeMeasure.title: Measurement data
whatWeMeasure.body:
The download test sends random bytes from our server to your browser. The upload test sends random bytes from your browser to our server, which discards them immediately without storing, reading or analysing them. Only the byte count is used.

Measurement results such as download speed and latency are not sent to our servers. Those figures are computed in your browser.

ipAddresses.title: IP addresses
ipAddresses.body:
Whenever a browser contacts a server, that server sees your IP address; this is true of every website and cannot be avoided. The Laju server uses that address only to return it to you in the connection panel.

Our application code does not write IP addresses to any database or log file.

thirdParties.title: Third-party services
thirdParties.body:
So that both IPv4 and IPv6 can be shown at once, your browser contacts two hostnames that each serve a single address family. Those services receive your IP address, because returning it is precisely what they do, and they have their own privacy policies.

The exact endpoints used by this deployment are listed on the Compliance page. Whoever runs the deployment can disable these lookups, in which case the connection panel shows only the address our own server sees.

Web fonts are loaded from Google Fonts, so your browser contacts that service while the page loads.

storage.title: Storage on your device
storage.body: Test history is kept in your browser's local storage, capped at the 30 most recent results. It is never sent to our servers and can be erased at any time with the button on the History page or by clearing site data in your browser.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: We use a single functional cookie to remember your language choice. There are no advertising cookies, no cross-site tracking and no device fingerprinting.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.body: As of the last update to this document, the site runs no third-party analytics. If that changes, this page and the Compliance page will be updated before such a service is enabled.

children.title: Children
children.body: The service is aimed at a general audience and is not designed specifically for children. Because there are no accounts and no profiling, we do not knowingly collect personal data from children.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body:
Because we hold no data that identifies you, there is no personal archive we could export or delete on request. What exists sits on your device and is entirely under your control.

If you would still like to check something, please get in touch through the Contact page.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: Any change to how measurement, storage or third-party services work comes with an update to this page and its revision date.

contact.title: Contacting us
contact.body: Questions about this policy can be sent through the Contact page.

acceptance.title: Acceptance
acceptance.body: By using Laju you agree to the terms on this page. If you do not agree with them, please do not use the service.

service.title: What the service provides
service.body: Laju provides browser-based connection measurements and displays technical information about your connection. It is offered free of charge and without accounts.

accuracy.title: Nature of the results
accuracy.body:
Results are indicative. The figures describe the path between your browser and a single test server at the time of the run, and are affected by your device, your local network and the load on the network at that moment.

Laju results are not intended as formal evidence in a dispute with your internet service provider.

acceptableUse.title: Acceptable use
acceptableUse.body:
The measurement endpoints exist for people testing through this site's interface. Please do not run high-volume automated testing, place excessive load on the service, or use it as a traffic source for other purposes.

We may rate-limit or block requests that harm availability for other people.

availability.title: Availability
availability.body: The service may pause for maintenance, updates or problems at our infrastructure provider. We do not promise any particular level of availability.

intellectualProperty.title: Content rights
intellectualProperty.body: The name, design and written content of this site belong to the project maintainer. Your own measurement results are yours to use and share freely.

liability.title: Limitation of liability
liability.body: The service is provided as is. To the extent permitted by applicable law, we are not liable for losses arising from use or unavailability of the service, including decisions made on the basis of a measurement.

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: This document covers the Laju site and its measurement endpoints. It is an explanation, not a certification: we claim no third-party audit or accreditation.

dataMinimisation.title: Data minimisation
dataMinimisation.body: The service is designed to work without accounts, without mandatory forms, and without storing results on a server. The test payload is random bytes that contain nothing about you and are discarded on arrival.

ipDisclosure.title: Openness about IP addresses
ipDisclosure.body:
A web page cannot ask the operating system for its IP addresses. All it can do is ask a server which address that server saw.

Because a single server only ever sees one address family, showing IPv4 and IPv6 together requires the browser to contact two different hostnames. We say so explicitly rather than presenting the result as if it came from your device.

thirdParties.title: Third parties
thirdParties.body: This deployment uses the address-lookup endpoints listed above and loads web fonts from Google Fonts. There is no ad network, no cross-site tracker and no other third-party embed on the page.

measurementHonesty.title: Measurement honesty
measurementHonesty.body:
The engine parameters shown on the How It Works page are read directly from the program's configuration, so the documentation cannot drift from actual behaviour.

The limits of the method are listed on the same page. Activity estimates such as streaming or video calling are labelled as estimates, not guarantees.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.body:
The interface aims to follow common practice: adequate contrast, visible keyboard focus, a skip link, semantic elements and respect for reduced-motion preferences.

We have not carried out a formal accessibility audit, so we do not claim a specific WCAG conformance level. Reports of accessibility problems are very welcome.

security.title: Security
security.body:
The site is served over HTTPS. Measurement endpoints enforce request size limits and return headers that forbid caching, so a cache in the middle cannot fake a result.

Because there is no user database, there is no credential store or personal history that could leak from our side.

openness.title: Openness
openness.body: The method, parameters and limits are written openly on this site. If you find a mismatch between what is written and what happens, tell us and we will follow it up and update this page.

limitations.title: Limits we acknowledge
limitations.body:
We do not operate a global network of test servers, so a result does not always represent the path to other services. We also depend on the hosting provider for infrastructure-level logs that sit outside our code.

We hold no ISO, SOC or comparable certification, and we display no compliance badge we do not have.
